source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New York's entire published data center capacity is 3 MW, at one CyrusOne facility in Wappingers Falls, which says more about disclosure than about the grid.

The facility publishes 3 MW of IT capacity and 100,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that load is roughly 75 racks. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so the actual deployment is not documented. The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers audited controls for hosting services and says nothing about AI workloads.

For AI specifically, the published record is silent on the things that decide whether accelerators can run at a site: liquid cooling, high-density power delivery, and substation and interconnection arrangements. On what is published, this is a general colocation facility, and any AI use of it is undocumented. That gap matters because compute scaling is constrained by power delivery and buildings, and neither can be assessed from a capacity figure alone.

The state ranking should not be read as a measure of buildout. This campus ranks first in New York by published megawatts, but it is the only facility in the state with a published MW figure, out of 31 mapped facilities. Its 3 MW is the entire published total for New York. The mapped footprint is far larger than the disclosed capacity, so the ranking reflects disclosure practice, not the grid.
